schemaNote: Provisional shape; final schema owned by issue #11.

tiers.community-reference: Statements from the community guide at the pinned revision. authority=community-maintained.

constraints.statement: The AE scripting engine implements ECMA-262 3rd Edition and also implements E4X (ECMA-357).
constraints.implication: Language features from ES5 and later (let/const, arrow functions, Array.prototype.map, JSON, getters) must not be assumed present in host-side script. A codec that transpiles to ES3 is required rather than optional.

constraints.statement: The documented keyword and operator tables describe only ES3 syntax; ES5+ statements are absent from the supported language surface.
constraints.implication: Syntax support must be validated against the ES3 operator/keyword table, not against a generic JavaScript parser configured for an older target.

constraints.statement: Adobe states the AE 16.0+ JavaScript *expression* engine is ECMAScript 2018 while the *legacy* expression engine is ECMAScript 3. This is a statement about the expression engine, not about the ExtendScript scripting engine.
constraints.implication: Do not infer that scripting gained ES2018 features. The two engines are separate and the ingestion path must not share a syntax assumption with the expression path.

constraints.statement: Scripts share one global environment: variables and functions defined by a script persist into later scripts within the same AE session and are cleared when AE quits.
constraints.implication: Globals are a cross-call state channel. A dispatcher must reclaim or namespace its own globals every call, or a second call can observe a previous call's state.

constraints.statement: Collection indexing starts at 1, not 0, and collection membership updates automatically as objects are created or deleted.
constraints.implication: An index is a position, not an identity. Any handle scheme keyed on an index is invalidated by insertion, deletion or reordering.

constraints.statement: Some classes exist only as base classes; `instanceof` against them either returns false or throws because the class name is undefined.
constraints.implication: Type checks performed by an adapter must target the most specific class, and must tolerate undefined class names rather than assuming `instanceof` is total.

constraints.statement: beginUndoGroup/endUndoGroup pairs nest; nested groups join the outer group and inner group names are discarded. An unmatched endUndoGroup is an error.
constraints.implication: A script that opens a group and fails before closing it changes the undo semantics of the whole session. Write operations need a finally-style close.

constraints.statement: If a script never calls endUndoGroup, the system closes the group automatically at the end of the script.
constraints.implication: Undo grouping is script-scoped by default, so splitting one logical operation across two script invocations creates two undo steps unless grouping spans them.

constraints.statement: The purge API exposes an UNDO_CACHES target, so undo history is a purgeable host resource.
constraints.implication: Purging undo caches discards recovery state. It must never be used as a cleanup step after a failed mutation.

constraints.statement: Error dialog suppression is explicitly begun and ended by the script; suppression does not extend beyond the call pair.
constraints.implication: Headless execution depends on suppressing dialogs, but suppression covers error dialogs only. A modal panel or alert raised by a script is not covered by this pair.

constraints.statement: Scripts in the ScriptUI Panels folder behave like dockable AE panels and appear at the bottom of the Window menu.
constraints.implication: A panel-based adapter runs inside the AE UI event loop. Blocking the UI thread from a panel is a user-visible failure mode, not a background stall.

constraints.statement: Scripts may not write files by default; a Scripting & Expressions preference must be enabled.
constraints.implication: A file-transport bridge (write request, read result) fails closed on a default install. Permission state must be discovered and reported, not assumed.

constraints.statement: Network send/receive is disabled by default and is gated by the same single preference as file writing.
constraints.implication: File and network permission cannot be requested independently. Enabling socket transport necessarily also enables file writes.

constraints.statement: Pressing Esc stops a running script.
constraints.implication: Any long host operation is interruptible by a human at any point, so a partial mutation is always reachable and cleanup cannot be assumed to run.

constraints.statement: The documented command-line script invocation runs in the already-running AE instance instead of starting a new one.
constraints.osScope: statement is OS-neutral; the example uses the Windows afterfx.exe path
constraints.implication: Invoking a script from the command line does not isolate the run from a user's open project. Session ownership must be established separately.

constraints.statement: A script added to the Scripts folder while AE is running needs an AE restart before it appears in the menu, though Run Script File works immediately.
constraints.implication: Installing an adapter by copying it into the Scripts folder requires a restart cycle; loading it per-invocation avoids that lifecycle cost.

constraints.statement: The permission preference is reached through different menu paths on Windows (Edit > Preferences) and macOS (After Effects > Settings).
constraints.implication: A guidance string for enabling permissions is OS-specific. A single message is wrong on one platform.

constraints.statement: The exitAfterLaunchAndEval attribute only has an effect when AE is launched from the Windows command line and has no effect on Mac OS.
constraints.osScope: Windows only; explicitly no effect on Mac OS
constraints.implication: Fire-and-exit behaviour is not portable. A launcher must not depend on this attribute to reap a headless run on macOS.

constraints.statement: The exit code is returned on the Windows command line but as an AppleScript DoScript result on Mac OS.
constraints.osScope: Windows command line vs macOS AppleScript
constraints.implication: Exit status is not a portable success channel. A result envelope must carry its own status rather than relying on process exit.

constraints.statement: system.osName returns a blank value on Windows 7 and later; the guide directs scripts to $.os instead.
constraints.implication: OS detection must not trust system.osName. Host identity reported through this attribute is unreliable on modern Windows.

constraints.statement: Property values are typed by PropertyValueType; spatial values are float arrays, colors are four floats, shapes and text documents are host objects.
constraints.implication: A generic JSON codec cannot round-trip every value: host objects such as Shape and TextDocument have no documented plain-data form, so they need per-type adapters or must be refused.

constraints.statement: The integer values behind guide orientationType and positionType differ between AE versions; scripts must compare against the named constants, not raw integers.
constraints.aeVersionScope: changed at 26.5; prior versions expose plain integers
constraints.implication: An enum wire encoding that serialises the integer rather than the name is not stable across AE versions. Enum values must travel as names.
